subject: CAIQ control mapping: runtime feature ownership index & evidence rendezvous
messages:
From: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@heliohealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
Cc: audits@heliohealth.com
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ runtime control clarifications and sample evidence window

Jonas,

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. As HelioHealth's security team prepares for a targeted CSA/CAIQ review focused on runtime protections, we need a compact crosswalk that maps CAIQ control IDs to the runtime features in your private deployment offering (prefix/KV cache, per-tenant isolation, autoscaling policies, auditing hooks).

Specifically can you provide: 
- A control->feature mapping (one row per CAIQ control with the corresponding runtime component and owner)
- A short list of representative evidence items we can use for sampling (log samples, KV cache TTL config, autoscaler policy JSON)
- Preferred time window for sampling (2 business days preferred) and point of contact from your side for live access/questions

We'd like to start the sampling on Monday 10 May if possible. Delivery target for the crosswalk and evidence list: COB Friday 7 May.

Appreciate your help — if there are any controls you consider out-of-scope for HelioHealth's tenancy model, flag them with rationale.

Best,
Liam O'Connell
Security Lead, HelioHealth
-----
From: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
To: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@heliohealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ runtime control clarifications and sample evidence window

Liam — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Short answers up front: yes, we can deliver a compact crosswalk + sampling list by COB Fri (7 May), and Monday 10 May works for a two-day live sampling window.

Action plan (high level):
- I will attach a first-pass control->runtime crosswalk (CAIQ control id -> runtime component -> evidence candidates -> owner). Kimberly will own the evidence bundling and produce the sample artifacts; Marissa will coordinate DocuSign/access approvals with your audit team.
- We'll mark controls that are tenant-specific (i.e., HelioHealth's isolation posture) vs platform-level (shared infra) and provide short rationales where a control is not directly applicable.

Attachments: CAIQ_runtime_ownership_crosswalk_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) — draft

Next steps for you: confirm the sampling window (10–11 May) and share any on-call contact for urgent questions during the live sample. We'll follow up with a secure upload link for evidence and a DocuSign for access acceptance.

Jonas Weber
Sr. Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

+1 — uploaded the evidence candidates and added notes in the crosswalk. Key points: 
- The crosswalk includes a runtime "ownership" column that references internal stewards (serving-runtime, infra, secops). Where HelioHealth requires tenant-scoped artifacts, I added a recommended extraction filter (tenant_id=hl-4821).
- Evidence bundle (zipped): authz-audit.log (last 7 days slice), kv-cache-config.json (TTL and eviction policy), autoscaler-policy-202704.json, sample-kv-ttl-query.sql (redacted).
- Sampling constraints: to preserve perf, we recommend two 2-hour windows (UTC 02:00–04:00 and UTC 16:00–18:00) across two days; these windows minimize impact but still capture typical traffic patterns. If HelioHealth requires business-hours traces, we can expand to daytime sampling but will need a brief maintenance window.

Attachments included in this thread: evidence-sample-list.zip, sampling-schedule.pdf

Notes for Marissa: please prep a short access-acceptance DocuSign for HelioHealth and a scoped SFTP/upload link for the evidence bundle.

-Kim
